doc.title: Gordon Lorraine — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: In the control booth and listening to acetates
summary: Gordon sat in on sessions at WOR studio, then she and Alfred and Ike listened to acetate test pressings at home on Grove Street.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: So you were in the control booth during the recording sessions.
Yeah. I was listening in. Not that I could tell them what to do or what not to do. But I was there to hear if anything went wrong, that I could throw up my hands in despair or something.
But also, you and Alfred would go home with the tapes.

Oh, the tests. The test pressings. My gosh. Yes, we would take them home. Ike would come over very often and listen with us. We sat in our couch in our little one-room apartment down there on Grove Street, and we listened to those early... They weren’t tapes. They were acetates, big acetates. And we had a little skimpy box we played it on. When I think of the equipment today and what we listened on! It was a square box. It had a radio on the bottom and a turntable on the top, and we put the records on there, and we hovered around that box, listening to every sound. It was beautiful. We didn’t know anything better. We thought that was great.
